title: Unity of Scripture
definition: The unity of Scripture means that the many books of the Bible form one coherent divine testimony because one God speaks through them.
summary: Scripture contains many human authors, genres, and settings, yet it presents one unfolding story of creation, fall, redemption, and restoration.
christFocus: The unity of Scripture is fulfilled in Christ, who is the center of God's saving purpose.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content: Unity of Scripture teaches that God's people must receive this truth under the authority of the Lord, allowing Scripture itself to define the doctrine rather than personal opinion, tradition, or culture.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: This doctrine matters because it protects the believer from confusion and helps the church remain anchored in what God has actually spoken. Without this truth, faith can drift toward feelings, assumptions, or human wisdom.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: A disciple should respond to unity of scripture by reading the Word prayerfully, testing beliefs by Scripture, obeying what God reveals, and helping others handle the Bible with humility, clarity, and faith.

studySections.heading: Guardrails and Common Errors
studySections.content: This doctrine should not be used to win arguments while neglecting love, nor should it be separated from prayer, obedience, and dependence on the Holy Spirit. The goal is faithful submission to God, not mere possession of information.

sources: Scripture references listed in this doctrine entry.
